deviation: The draft replaces Arcadia's unconditional annual audit right on 14 days' notice with a tiered process: the Supplier first provides information and third-party reports, and a direct audit is allowed only if that is insufficient, a regulator requires it, or a Security Incident has occurred. It also gives no fixed notice period ("reasonable notice") and no set frequency. This is weaker than the standard and the fallback (one audit every two years), because Arcadia can no longer audit routinely and the Supplier can argue its reports are enough.
suggested_text: The Supplier shall make available to the Customer the information reasonably necessary to demonstrate compliance with this Addendum, including current third-party audit reports or certifications it holds. In addition, the Customer, or an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, may audit the Supplier's records and facilities relevant to this Addendum once per year on 14 days' notice, during normal business hours and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt the Supplier's operations. The Customer may also audit at any time on reasonable notice where a regulator requires it or a Security Incident has occurred. Providing information or reports does not limit the Customer's right to audit. Each party bears its own costs of an audit, unless the audit reveals a material breach by the Supplier, in which case the Supplier shall bear the Customer's reasonable costs.
